claim: ATT&CK is the common language for attacker behaviour.
quote: Such a knowledge base provides security professionals with a common language for understanding, categorizing, and mitigating cyber threats.
issue: Büchel uses the same words, and also calls it "the de facto standard for structuring TTPs" (same page).

claim: Automated attack profiling scales to many reports.
quote: information on TTPs is often only given in unstructured form as part of human-written textual CTI reports, which must be manually analyzed and extracted. As the volume and complexity of CTI reports increase
issue: Büchel gives report volume as the reason to automate. It does not state or measure that the automated systems scale. This is an inference, and a reasonable one.

claim: Even identifying which techniques a report describes is not yet reliable.
quote: Even with prior knowledge of the test dataset, the results of all experiments are far from being fully reliable automatic annotation systems for practical use.
locator: p. 4634 printed (PDF p. 15), discussion, "Are We There Yet?"

claim: On the 50 most common techniques, the best systems reach 80 % precision at 66 % recall.
quote: even when considering only the top-50 most common TTPs, the best-performing solutions reach a precision of around 80% for a recall of around 66%
locator: p. 4622 printed (PDF p. 3), Sect. 1 key insight 1; Table 12, p. 4632 printed (PDF p. 13): "Generation 72.50 80.00 66.30"
issue: Numbers checked exactly. Table 12 (TRAM2, which "encompasses the 50 most frequently observed techniques") gives 80.00 % precision and 66.30 % recall, so dropping the source's "around" is safe. That best result is from the favourable closed-set scenario, where the data is known in advance. Leaving that out only understates the sentence's point.
